United ISD board members-elect Victor Vasquez and Leticia “Lety” Juarez say they will focus on district finances, audits, and clearer communication with parents when they are sworn in on Wednesday, November 11, according to KGNS.

Vasquez, the District 3 board member-elect, and Juarez, the District 5 board member-elect, begin serving immediately after taking the oath, KGNS reported.

Juarez said her priorities include reviewing the district's finances and finding other ways to cut spending, and she said she does not want any more schools closed — she opposed the first two closures, according to KGNS. She also wants to examine oversight and communication after recent lawsuits involving students with special needs, saying the checks and balances failed and it was a communication failure, and she wants to know who was not monitoring the aide involved.

Vasquez said he wants to commission a financial audit and review district contracts, running an efficient audit to understand the district's finances and find where it can cut costs and save, according to KGNS. He said he would stay away from the compensation plan. He also wants to give parents clearer information about their rights and complaint procedures, with faster communication between schools, the superintendent, and the board — communication, he said, is key.

A third trustee, Michelle Molina, was reelected in District 6 but was not available for an interview, so no priorities were reported for her, KGNS reported.

Sources: KGNS, November 9, 2026.

title: Incoming UISD trustees outline priorities ahead of Nov. 11 swearing-in
